newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - March 25.
newsitem.headline: PRESS DIGEST - Sri Lanka Newspapers - March 25.

text.p: These are the leading stories in the Sri Lankan press on Tuesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
Widespread rigging at last week's election for local councils, an independent monitoring groups says. The ruling People's Alliance (PA) coalition won the election by a landslide.
Navy destroys 10 Liberation Tigers of Tamil Eelam (LTTE) boats, killing more than 100 "Sea Tiger" guerrillas, off the coast of northeastern Mullaitivu.
Palestinian President Yasser Arafat says he is prepared to mediate to end Sri Lanka's 13-year-old war with the LTTE. Arafat is in Sri Lanka for a two-day official visit.
Government imports six billion rupees ($105 million) worth of textile material for free school uniforms for children in 1997.
An LTTE missile may have brought down an air force Mi-24 helicpoter gunship, which went missing off the coast of northeastern Mullaitivu on March 19, government investigators tell air force.
The PA's sweeping victory in last week's local council election was an endorsement of its two-and-a-half-year rule by the people, diplomats say.
Colombo gives red carpet welcome to Palestinian leader Yasser Arafat, who is on his first visit to the Indian Ocean island.
Eleven of the 20 suspects in police custody in connection with last month's killing of PA legislator Nalanda Ellawela released on bail by Ratnapura chief magistrate.
Chief suspects, main oppsition United National Party (UNP) lawmaker Susantha Punchinilame and former UNP mayor Mahinda Ratnatilleke, refused bail.
